{{Quote|Life is the enemy. Death is our solace.|Darth Marr's creed|<ref name="Encyclopedia" />}}
'''Darth Marr''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] and a member of the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituted Sith Empire's]] ruling [[Dark Council]] during the [[Great Galactic War]], [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], and [[Galactic War]] with the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. A fearsome warrior and stalwart defender of the Empire, Darth Marr was born in [[3702 BBY]] and assumed a seat on the Dark Council in his early twenties, leading the [[Sphere of Defense of the Empire]] as he drove back entire armies and halted Republic offensives during the Great War. By the end of the war in [[3653 BBY]], Marr had trained an apprentice by the name of [[Darth Lachris]] to the rank of [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] and was one of only seven remaining Councilors. He continued to strengthen Imperial defenses and prepare for the inevitable conflict throughout the Cold War, distancing himself from the power plays and treachery that plagued the Council and weakened the Empire.

As war broke out with the Republic, Marr watched as the Dark Council's numbers dwindled thanks to both the enemy and internal feuding, and he assumed a leadership role alongside fellow Councilors [[Darth Mortis]] and [[Darth Ravage]] after the deaths of [[Darth Baras]] and [[Darth Decimus]], the heads of the [[Sphere of Military Offense|Spheres of Military Offense]] and [[Sphere of Military Strategy|Military Strategy]], left him in sole command of the [[Imperial Military (Sith Empire)|Imperial Military]]. In doing so, he was seen as the de-facto leader of the Empire up until his [[Death/Legends|death]].

==Biography==
===Early career===
{{Quote|Your place is not to think. It is to hunt.|Darth Marr to Teneb Kel|<ref name="Blood of the Empire 1">''[[The Old Republic, Blood of the Empire Act 1: Shades of the Sith]]''</ref>}}
A [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]], the individual later known as [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Marr was born in [[3702 BBY]] in the territory of the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|resurgent Sith Empire]]. However, Marr's history was shrouded in secrecy: anyone who possessed knowledge of his past refused to reveal anything they knew after the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] came to power. Trained as a [[Sith Warrior]], Marr adopted an armored battle suit like many powerful Sith, and Marr's armor and emotionless mask were designed to invoke the idea of a monstrous [[Sithspawn/Legends|Sithspawn]] creature.<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> Marr recovered the [[Tulak Hord's lightsaber|lightsaber]] of the ancient [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] Lord [[Tulak Hord]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Dromund Fels]] shortly before his ascension to the Sith Empire's ruling Dark Council,<ref name="Legacy">{{TORcite|type=codex|Legacy of Tulak Hord}}</ref> a position that he achieved sometime around the beginning of the [[Great Galactic War]] with the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]<ref name="Blood of the Empire 1" /> in [[3681 BBY]].<ref name="Timeline 1">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 1: Treaty of Coruscant|int=Timeline 1: Treaty of Coruscant}}</ref> Like the other eleven members of the Council, Marr headed one of the Empire's [[Spheres of Influence]]&mdash;in Marr's case, the [[Sphere of Defense of the Empire]].<ref name="Encyclopedia" />

[[File:Calypho_captured.png|thumb|left|250px|Darth Marr arrests Calypho.]]
Around [[3678 BBY]], Darth Marr and several other Dark Councilors confronted the Sith Lord [[Calypho]] on the world of [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]], arresting him for heresy just as Calypho's apprentice [[Darth Thanaton|Teneb Kel]] returned from a mission into the planet's ancient tombs. Kel was allowed to participate in the Imperial offensive on [[Begeren]], but after the [[Invasion of Begeren]] ended the apprentice was arrested as well. Darth Marr led parades in the streets of [[Kaas City]] on the Imperial capital of [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]] in celebration of the victory, but he afterwards attended a meeting of the Council in their [[Dark Council chamber (Dromund Kaas)|chamber]] beneath the [[Imperial Citadel (Sith Empire)|Imperial Citadel]]. There, Kel was brought before Darth Marr and the other Dark Councilors and ordered to [[Death/Legends|kill]] Lord Calypho. Marr noticed that the young Sith drew strength from his fear, causing another Councilor to mock Kel for not drawing upon his anger. When a Councilor halted the battle before Calypho's death, the Sith was taken away by [[Imperial Guard]]smen to be tortured, and Marr reminded the apprentice that he was not special&mdash;his master had made him into a disgrace.<ref name="Blood of the Empire 1" />

However, Marr and several other Councilors recognized that Kel could still be of use as a weapon, and Marr revealed a [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]] of the apprentice's target: [[Exal Kressh]], the wayward apprentice of the [[Tenebrae|Sith Emperor]]. The Dark Councilor brushed aside Kel's questions, informing the young Human that his place in the Empire would be judged again ''if'' he succeeded in the mission. He then brought Kel before the Emperor himself, bowing low as the Sith ruler informed Marr's chosen [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]] that Kressh could be found in the [[Lenico system/Legends|Lenico system]].<ref name="Blood of the Empire 1" /> Kel would eventually successfully track down and kill Kressh on Korriban, though not before learning that the Emperor intended to create his [[Children of the Emperor|Children]]&mdash;extensions of his will that would spread his influence secretly across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="Blood of the Empire 2">''[[The Old Republic, Blood of the Empire Act 2: The Broken World]]''</ref> During the young Human's report to the Dark Council, he refused to submit to their authority and prompted Darth Marr to summon a storm of [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]] as a threat. However, Kel convinced the Council to accept his offer: in exchange for information on the Emperor's plans, the Dark Council would grant him the rank of Sith Lord and the title of Darth Thanaton.<ref name="Blood of the Empire 3">''[[The Old Republic, Blood of the Empire Act 3: Burn the Future]]''</ref>

===Defender of the Empire===
{{Quote|My 'vision' is of an Empire ready to fight across the battlefield of life. That is all I require.|Darth Marr|<ref name="TOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Darth_Marr_leads_a_celebration.png|thumb|right|250px|Darth Marr was famous to the people of the Empire as their stalwart defender.]]
As the Great Galactic War continued, Darth Marr attained a fearsome reputation among both the Republic and the Empire, leading Imperial forces into battle and defending the Empire's conquests against Republic counterattacks with fearless determination.<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> In [[3660 BBY]],<ref name="Book of Sith">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref> Darth Marr drove back a [[Battle of Korriban (3660 BBY)|Republic offensive]] against Korriban, and he dealt the enemy another grievous defeat when the Republic attempted to [[Battle of Ziost|strike at]] [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]].<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> By the end of the war, Marr had trained an apprentice of his own in [[Darth Lachris]], who was a fierce warrior at heart who understood the bitter necessity of politics like her master.<ref name="Lachris" /> He also took an interest in certain [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] individuals within the Empire, such as the [[Talos Drellik's brother|brother]] of [[Talos Drellik]], and would often personally take them to the [[Sith Academy (Korriban)|Sith Academy]] on Korriban.<ref name="Talos Drellik">{{TORcite|type=conversation|Talos Drellik|Force Sensitivity}}</ref> Marr was known throughout the Republic as the masked Dark Councilor who had defeated entire armies and halted dozens of Republic assaults,<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> and he was one of only seven members of the Dark Council who was still alive by the time<ref name="The Lost Suns 1">[[The Old Republic — The Lost Suns 1|''The Old Republic — The Lost Suns'' 1]]</ref> the [[Treaty of Coruscant]] ended the war in [[3653 BBY]].<ref name="Timeline 1" />

Over the next decade&mdash;a time that became known as the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]]&mdash;Darth Marr devoted himself to preparing the Empire for the next conflict, strengthening Imperial defenses and exerting control over his Sphere of Influence to ensure that the Republic would find no cracks in the armor of the Empire. After [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Xerxian]] failed to quell an [[Sullust uprising|uprising]] on the Imperial-[[Battle of Sullust (Great Galactic War)|conquered]] world of [[Sullust/Legends|Sullust]], the man was summoned to a private audience with Darth Marr. After the meeting, Xerxian dictated a letter of resignation and shot himself, leading to many rumors about what had happened. The most predominant one was that the Sith Lord had removed his mask and allowed Xerxian to view his supposedly ruined face.<ref name="Encyclopedia" />

[[File:MechaBeehiveAndRevanWannabe-SWTOR2TLS2.png|thumb|left|250px|Darth Marr and Darth Mekhis were two Dark Councilors who survived the war.]]
When the prototype Imperial warship ''[[Voidstar]]'' was rediscovered, Marr ordered an Imperial strike team to reclaim the vessel before the Republic could capture the derelict dreadnaught.<ref name="Voidstar">{{TORcite|Warzone: "''Voidstar''"}}</ref> Governor [[Lysennius Melchiro]]'s<ref name="Stepping Lightly">{{TORcite|type=faction|Imperial|Stepping Lightly|Balmorra}}</ref> continued failure to suppress the [[Balmorran resistance]] on the conquered planet [[Balmorra/Legends|Balmorra]] eventually led to his removal by the Dark Council, and Marr's former apprentice Darth Lachris was selected to take Melchiro's place.<ref name="Toxic Bombs">{{TORcite|type=heroic|Toxic Bombs|Balmorra}}</ref> After a Republic assault on the world failed, Lachris' forces captured a large number of [[Republic trooper]]s and several [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], and the Sith Lord delivered the captive Jedi to Darth Marr so that the Dark Councilor could attempt to break the prisoners and convert them to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]].<ref name="Breaking the Resistance">{{TORcite|type=faction|Imperial|Breaking the Resistance|Balmorra}}</ref>

===Infighting and open war===
In [[3640 BBY]],<ref name="Time">{{TOR dates|4}}</ref> Darth Marr was presented with the body of [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Dorian Janarus]] by [[Darth Tormen]] during a special session of the Council, as Tormen's [[Hunter (individual)|bounty hunter]] had [[Assassin/Legends|assassinated]] the Chancellor aboard his personal cruiser [[Founder (Valor-class)|''Founder'']] during the [[Battle of Corellia]]. Marr was pleased with Tormen's work, and expressed an interest in hiring the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] if the need arose later on. Marr's support infuriated his fellow Dark Councilor [[Darth Decimus]], whose [[Sphere of Military Strategy]] had planned the Imperial invasion of Corellia and who was personally overseeing the battle.<ref name="You have served well">{{TORcite|type=message|You have served well|Darth Tormen}}</ref>

[[File:DarthMarrSeat001.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Darth Marr in his seat on the Dark Council]]
Not long afterwards, Darth Marr and the other Councilors were summoned to Korriban by fellow Dark Councilor [[Darth Baras]]. [[Darth Hadra|Darths Hadra]] and [[Darth Acharon|Acharon]] were forced to attend via [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]] with Decimus, as the two had joined Decimus in overseeing the Imperial offensive on [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]]. At the meeting, Baras attempted to declare himself [[Emperor's Voice (Sith Empire)|Voice of the Emperor]]&mdash;the individual through whom the Emperor delivered his commands&mdash;and therefore take control of the entire Empire, but Baras was interrupted by the arrival of [[Darth Vowrawn]] and Baras' [[Empire's Wrath|former apprentice]]. The Sith Warrior had been appointed as the [[Emperor's Wrath]], and Marr reprimanded [[Darth Ravage]] when his fellow Councilor agreed to Baras' request that the Council kill his former student. Declaring the Wrath's challenge was valid and supported by Vowrawn, one of the Council's own members, Marr pitted Baras and his student against each other: whichever was victorious would be acknowledged by the Council as a true servant of the Emperor. As Marr and the other Councilors watched from their seats, the Wrath battled the false Voice in a [[Duel in the Dark Council Chambers (Galactic War)|duel]] within the [[Dark Council Chambers|Council chamber]]. But as Baras began to falter, he appealed to Darth Marr to defend the Emperor's Voice, but Marr refused. Ravage did the same when Baras ordered him to attack, and a defiant Baras was forced to confront the Wrath to prove his power before the Dark Council until his former student defeated him. Marr then led the rest of the Dark Council in acknowledging the Wrath's position and right to free reign, but hinted that the Council would not take kindly to actions that contradicted their own designs.<ref name="Retribution" />

After Baras' body was removed from the chamber, Darth Thanaton&mdash;recently ascended to the Council after the suspicious death of his predecessor [[Darth Arctis]]&mdash;rose to address his fellow Dark Lords. He appealed to the other Dark Councilors to aid him in destroying his rival and subordinate Lord [[Darth Nox|Kallig]], whom Thanaton had recently declared a [[Kaggath]] upon. The [[Kaggath (Galactic War)|Kaggath]], an ancient Sith ritual duel, had ended on [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] when Thanaton had fled to Korriban to meet with the Council, and Thanaton was angered to see that Kallig had followed him to Korriban when the young [[Sith Inquisitor]] entered the chamber. [[Darth Mortis]] and Ravage mocked Thanaton's reliance on ancient tradition, and Marr cut short the Councilor's speech by bringing up the matter at hand: why was Thanaton, a Dark Councilor, unable to kill a single Sith Lord? Furious, Thanaton began to [[Duel in the Dark Council Chambers (Kaggath)|duel]] Kallig, and their battle ended when the young Sith forced Thanaton to his knees in submission.

[[File:SithCocktailParty-TOR.png|thumb|left|250px|Darths Vowrawn, Marr, Mortis, and Ravage observe the fallen Thanaton]] As the drained Dark Councilor struggled to rise, Marr rose from his seat to join Ravage, Vowrawn, and Mortis in front of their fallen fellow, and they watched as Mortis broke Thanaton's neck to put him out of his misery. When Ravage expressed his disdain for Thanaton, Marr reprimanded his fellow Councilor, stating that Thanaton had been a better Sith than Ravage gave him credit for. The Councilors then offered Kallig with Thanaton's now empty seat; Ravage protested as they can't put just a Lord on the Council, but Marr silenced him as Kallig had earned the right. Marr named the young Inquisitor "Darth Nox" and bestowed the new Dark Councilor the [[Sphere of Ancient Knowledge]].<ref name="The Dark Council">{{TORcite|type=class|Sith Inquisitor|The Dark Council|Korriban}}</ref>

After the deaths of Decimus, Hadra, and Acharon and the Republic victory at Corellia,<ref name="Government Clearance">{{TORcite|type=faction|Republic|Government Clearance|Corellia}}</ref> Marr ordered [[General/Legends|General]] [[Hesker]] and all Imperial forces to retreat from the planet and redirect to the new battlefield of [[Ilum/Legends|Ilum]].<ref name="The Fall of Corellia">{{TORcite|type=faction|Imperial|The Fall of Corellia|Corellia}}</ref> Mortis, Ravage, and Marr also dispatched [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Ilyan Regus]] to Ilum.<ref name="The Final Front">{{TORcite|type=faction|Imperial|The Final Front|Ilum}}</ref> Around this time, the Dark Council met to discuss the successor to Hadra's seat on the council. Marr, who was full aware of the Empire's declining situation, nominated [[Darth Karrid]], and urged the other Councilors for their support since the Empire's soldiers and resources were dwindling. To his dismay, the other Councilors present supported [[Darth Gravus]], mainly due to the Empire's discrimination against non-humans. When Karrid killed Gravus, Marr was surprised by the Council's sudden decision change of support for Karrid, but also concluded that these recent actions were just another example of Sith infighting.

===The Empire on the brink===
[[File:Darth_Marr_-_Makeb.jpg|thumb|250px|Darth Marr during the Conquest of Makeb]]
In [[3638 BBY]] Marr gained word of the [[Hutt Cartel/Legends|Hutt Cartel's]] activities on the planet of [[Makeb]] and contacted the Empire's heroes to handle the threat. Upon meeting each of them individually, he explained that he had chosen them to deal with it because he had the rest of the war on his hands since the Emperor was still absent. With the Republic growing closer to victory, the Hutts had seized Makeb to mine [[isotope-5]], a substance capable of twisting gravitational and electromagnetic fields, making it a potent power source, which the Empire desperately needed for their defenses. Marr assigned a limited support team to assist the heroes, but warned them to proceed with stealth and avoid anything that could expose their intentions to the Hutts and the Republic.

Unfortunately, Marr was later displeased to learn that the Hutts had used all the available isotope-5 to create war droids and that their over-mining of Makeb's core threatened to tear the planet apart and the isotope with it. After stressing that three Imperial worlds had fallen to buy the Makeb team time, the latter managed to stabilize the planet's core and keep it secret from their enemies. After hearing of the success of the Empire's activities, Marr redesignated his whole focus onto the galactic war.

Soon after, the Empire had located the defected [[Dread Masters]]' base of operations on [[Oricon]]. Knowing that any plans of the now-rogue Masters were no good for anyone in the galaxy, Marr contacted the Empire's heroes once again and told them to look for Lord [[Hargrev]], who was supposed to have responded to Imperial comms. He told the heroes that the Dread Masters had to be stopped or everything would be lost.

===Against the Emperor===
[[File:DarthMarrRishi.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Darth Marr in the Raider's Cove on Rishi]]
The activities of the [[Nova Blades]] [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] working for the [[Order of Revan]] remapped the [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] lines, luring Darth Marr's fleet to [[Rishi/Legends|Rishi]] at the same time as the Republic forces under [[Satele Shan]]. The two fleets engaged each other but were interrupted when an associate of [[Lana Beniko]] revealed that the battle was orchestrated by the Revanite traitors aboard both fleets. Upon learning that [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] was still alive, Marr agreed to a temporary truce with Republic forces under the command of the [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] and met with Satele Shan in the town of [[Raider's Cove]] on Rishi's surface. Marr revealed to both the Republic and Imperial forces that he had become aware of the Emperor's plan to extinguish all life in the galaxy and that he had no wish to serve as a pawn for the Emperor's insanity. Marr explained that if Revan were to revive the Emperor as he planned to, everyone else would be unable to stop him from carrying out his plan to eradicate all life in the galaxy and that Revan had to be stopped from bringing the Emperor back from his incorporeal form. The combined fleets joined forces and traveled to [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]] where they established a coalition in order to spot Revan.

[[File:Darth_Marr_on_Yavin_4.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Darth Marr on Yavin 4]]
Upon setting up a base camp on the surface of Yavin 4, it became clear that the Republic and Imperial rank and file still did not trust each other and had to be convinced to stand against Revan together. Both Marr and Shan sensed a strong presence in the Force on the moon, which was neither the reborn Revan, nor the Emperor. After two sides established sensors enabling them to scout the area near the [[Temple of Sacrifice]], they picked up a signal which Marr recognized as belonging to the [[Imperial Guard]] training facility. Marr and Beniko detained Commandant [[Iven]] amidst the Revanites that ransacked the facility, after which Marr questioned him to discover more details about the Emperor and Revan's plans for him. The combined forces of the Republic and the Empire cleared the way to the Temple of Sacrifice, after which the most powerful members of the Coalition went to confront Revan directly.

[[File:Marr_Satele.png|thumb|left|250px|Darth Marr works with Satele Shan, Lana Beniko and Theron Shan.]]
In the final battle against Revan, Marr fought alongside Satele and [[Theron Shan]], Lana Beniko, [[Mandalore the Avenger|Shae Vizla]] and the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Jakarro]] for the future of all life in the galaxy. After a difficult fight and despite being temporarily overpowered by Revan throughout the fight, the group managed to defeat him. Despite their efforts, the Emperor returned to life, feeding on the deaths the Coalition caused among the Revanites, which greatly puzzled Marr, as the Emperor did not take a physical form or possess a body and left Yavin 4 as soon as he appeared. Revan reunited with his dark half and finally became one with the Force and in the aftermath of the fight Marr appointed Lana Beniko as the leader of the new [[Sith Intelligence]]. Darth Marr then rechristened the Emperor's Wrath as the new Wrath of the Empire and placed Darth Nox among the Elite of the Dark Council then proceeded to tell them that they were the only Sith Lords he could trust.

===Wild Space expedition===
{{Quote|It is ''you'' who fears death, "Valkorion". I do not. I will not kneel.|Darth Marr's defiant last words, to Emperor [[Tenebrae|Valkorion]]|audio=DarthMarr-Kneel.flac|<ref name="The Hunt" />}}
[[File:Darth_Marr_Defender_of_the_Empire.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Darth Marr prepares to defend his flagship.]]
Soon after the events on [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]], Darth Marr led a Republic and Imperial joint fleet into [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]] in search of both Vitiate and the unidentified invaders who had raided several planets of the two major galactic powers before then retreating back into unknown space. The fleet was composed of seven vessels, including Marr's own [[Darth Marr's flagship|destroyer]] as [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]]. Marr sensed he was getting closer to Vitiate and knew if he found him, he would get the Dark Council to send more forces although he doubted the Republic would contribute further, despite their useful assistance until then. Suddenly, the [[Eternal Fleet]] appeared in front of the Republic and Imperial forces and [[Destruction of Darth Marr's flagship|engaged them]], shooting several [[Boarding craft/Legends|boarding pods]] into the flagship. [[Skytrooper]]s, the enemy boarders, caused chaos across the entire ship as Darth Marr helped to protect the [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]]. Despite his efforts in trying to prevent the ship's loss, he eventually determined that there wasn't anything more he, or his companion, [[Alliance Commander|the Commander]], could do and asked the latter what to do next.

[[File:Darth_Marrs_death.png|thumb|left|250px|Marr was killed by his former Emperor in an incredible display of power.]]
After the loss of his ship and the respective battle, Marr and the Outlander were held captive aboard [[Prince/Legends|Prince]] [[Arcann]]'s [[Eternal Flagship|ship]] and taken to the [[Eternal Empire]]'s [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Zakuul]]. There, the prince brought them to his father, the empire's leader, [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Tenebrae|Valkorion]], who Darth Marr quickly understood to be just another identity of Vitiate. Marr and the Outlander revealed their purpose being there was to destroy Valkorion but the latter offered that they join him instead. Darth Marr bluntly refused Valkorion's offer and proceeded to attack and kill several of the Emperor's guards. Before Darth Marr could continue further, he received a direct hit of [[Force lightning/Legends|concentrated Force lightning]] from Valkorion's hand, killing the Sith Lord.<ref name="The Hunt" />

===Post-Mortem===
{{Quote|In life, I dismissed the Jedi Code. I was wrong. There is no death. There is only the Force. And it has a plan.|Marr's ghost to the Outlander, in the wilds of Odessen|audio=DarthMarr-JediCode.flac|<ref name="Chapter 12">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|chapter=12}}</ref>}}
[[File:Satele_Marr.png|thumb|right|250px|As a [[Force ghost/Legends|Force ghost]], Marr joined [[Satele Shan]] in her exile on [[Odessen]].]]
Though his physical body had died, Marr, unwilling to leave the Sith Empire undefended, became a [[Force ghost/Legends|Force ghost]]. Five years later, his spirit communed with Satele Shan as they sensed the presence of Valkorion. Later, they both traveled to [[Odessen]], the home base of the Outlander's [[Eternal Alliance|Alliance]], comprised of elements from both Empire and Republic, united against the Eternal Empire. Though Satele admired their commitment, Marr lamented that many would die in the war to come.<ref name="Chapter 9">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|chapter=9}}</ref>

Marr and Satele later happened upon the Outlander after the latter had received a portion of Valkorion's power, rendered unconscious as a result. The pair debated whether to spare or execute the Outlander, but ultimately decided on the former, seeing that the Outlander represented the last vestige of hope in the galaxy. Marr remained invisible as Satele interacted with the Outlander, eventually revealing himself as Satele described Arcann and the [[Knights of Zakuul]]'s views on the Force. Marr told the Outlander that to defeat Arcann, they needed to gain new perspectives and new weapons. As the Outlander collected a series of items throughout the valley, Marr counseled that defeating Arcann was not enough and said that the Outlander was destined to take the Eternal Throne to restore order to the galaxy, claiming that any other path would lead to chaos.

[[File:Darth_Marrs_Force_Ghost.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Darth Marr provides guidance to the Outlander.]]
After facing a vision of [[Vaylin]] in a dark cave, Marr cautioned that it was a warning from the Force that Arcann and Vaylin had an army at their command to face any who would oppose them. He then instructed the Outlander that their previous weapon was built for a different war and time and they would need to construct a new weapon that would unite the galaxy and ultimately defeat Arcann. After the weapon was constructed, Marr predicted that the Outlander would defeat Arcann in their next confrontation, but cautioned that leading the Alliance was far different than their previous role.

After the Outlander finished their final trial at the [[jurgoran]]'s oasis, Marr told the Outlander that the Alliance would collapse if the Outlander did not know who they were inside and the ideal they serve. Having given all they had to impart, Marr and Satele sensed a calling in the Force indicating that their exile on Odessen was over, and departed.<ref name="Chapter 12" />

===Destroying Tenebrae===
{{Quote|He is a relic of an era long past. Destroy him&mdash;break the chains he uses to ensnare us all. Free the galaxy from his manipulations. Avenge me. Avenge us all!|Marr to the Outlander, in Satele's mindscape|audio=DarthMarr-Mindscape.flac|<ref name="Echoes of Oblivion">{{TORcite|type=general|Echoes of Oblivion|Odessen}}</ref>}}
[[File:Darth_Marr_in_Echoes_of_Oblivion.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Darth Marr arrives to aid in the final defeat of Tenebrae.]]
In the year [[3626 BBY]]<ref name="6.2Date">{{TOR_updates|6.2}}</ref>, Marr reappeared to the Outlander in [[Mindscape|Satele's mind]], when they were attempting to prevent Tenebrae from resurrecting himself. Marr explained that Satele was much stronger than what the Sith Emperor had believed, and that she was not the easy prey he assumed her to be. He further explained that while the Emperor grows stronger by feeding off the memories and impressions of his former self from Satele and her followers, he possesses none of the wisdom gained by experiencing them, and though he was still the most dangerous being in the galaxy, Tenebrae was more vulnerable than he wanted his enemies to believe. Marr theorized that the [[Tenebrae's curse|ritual]] carved onto Tenebrae's original body must have been made centuries ago, likely before even Revan's time. When the Outlander moved to confront Tenebrae, Marr appeared alongside everyone else who had been victimized by Tenebrae over the centuries, and joined in the fight to finish off the Sith Emperor once and for all, proclaiming that the Sith will grow beyond him and that all his power cannot save him. With Tenebrae finally vanquished, Marr became [[Netherworld of the Force/Legends|one]] with the Force.<ref name="Echoes of Oblivion" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Marr actually gave your people real leadership. More than ''you'' ever did for them."<br />"He was narrow-minded... bound by irrelevant ancient dogma.|[[Alliance Commander|The Commander]] and Valkorion, moments after Marr's death|<ref name="The Hunt" />}}
[[File:Darth_Marr_ignites_lightsaber.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Darth Marr was a formidable warrior.]]
Darth Marr was a human male who was famous for never revealing his true face&mdash;the Dark Lord was perpetually encased in his personalized suit of battle armor, and rumor had it that the sight of Marr's visage was the reason [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Xerxian]] committed suicide. Marr chose to keep this appearance as a [[Force ghost/Legends|Force ghost]], wishing to be remembered as a symbol. Throughout his tenure on the [[Dark Council]], Darth Marr's body slowly transformed as a result of immersion in the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]], and by the time war broke out again with the Republic, the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] was aware that his body would not last much longer.<ref name="Encyclopedia" />

Marr was driven by a fierce dedication to warfare, one that bordered on zealotry. He believed that conflict was the only way that life evolved and grew stronger, and Marr's personal view was that death was inevitable&mdash;only cowards tried to avoid that which was a necessity. Darth Marr's power in the dark side gradually stripped him of emotion over the decades, leaving the man with a fraction of his humanity but a strong desire to ensure that the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Empire]] survived.<ref name="Encyclopedia" />

[[File:Darth_Marr_projects_authority.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Darth Marr's authority held the Sith Empire together in difficult times.]]
The Sith Lord understood that the Empire needed to evolve in order to survive, and he was frustrated by his fellow Councilors' bigotry and the way that they clung to the old anti-[[Alien/Legends|alien]] philosophies even after the Empire began opening its ranks to alien [[Species/Legends|species]] following the defeat of the traitorous [[Darth Malgus]] at the [[Battle of Ilum]].<ref name="Annihilation" /> In addition, Marr was different from most Sith who viewed the Jedi with contempt. Instead, he respected them as warriors and Force Wielders, even viewing Jedi [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] [[Satele Shan]] as the only one in the galaxy worthy of being his equal. Marr was also aware that the continuing of backstabbing and infighting would destroy the Empire and tried to keep it under control in the Emperor's absence. Marr was disappointed when Karrid chose to destroy Gravus for her own ends, which made her a Dark Councilor, but made the Empire more vulnerable.

Marr developed a great deal of respect for [[Darth Thanaton]], telling Ravage that he was a better Sith than Ravage gave him credit for, and also telling [[Darth Nox]] that he had never thought to see the day Thanaton would fall.

Following his death, Marr acknowledged that his unbendable resolve made him brittle and developed a new interpretation of the Force, acknowledging the truth in the final mantra of the [[Jedi Code/Legends|Jedi code]], "There is no death, there is only the Force", and that it had a plan.

==Powers and abilities==
[[File:Marr_lightning.png|thumb|left|120px|Darth Marr summons Force lightning.]]
A Sith Warrior, Darth Marr was a remarkably powerful practitioner of the dark side; his strength was such that he ascended to a seat on the Dark Council while still in his early twenties.<ref name="Encyclopedia" /><ref name="Blood of the Empire 1" /> He was able to maintain his position over the next forty years while the tenure of some Councilors lasted mere weeks. Even Emperor Vitiate saw the potential threat that Darth Marr as well as Darth Mortis had on his throne. He wielded a single red-bladed [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] in combat while protected by his specialized suit of Sith battle armor, and his prowess in battle was such that he had a reputation for routing entire armies, and some stated that the Dark Council member was more effective than a [[Planetary shield/Legends|Planetary Defense Shield]].<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> During a spar with Darth Lachris, Marr shown enough speed to seemingly have "teleported" in Darth Lachris' eyes. Darth Marr was also skilled in using [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]], as he was able to summon a crackling storm of lightning at a moment's notice in order to threaten the impudent Teneb Kel.<ref name="Blood of the Empire 3" />

==Behind the scenes==
Darth Marr first appeared in ''[[The Old Republic, Blood of the Empire Act 1: Shades of the Sith]]'', the fourth issue of the [[Star Wars: The Old Republic (comic series)|''Star Wars: The Old Republic'' comic series]] and the first in the [[Star Wars: The Old Republic, Blood of the Empire|''Blood of the Empire'']] arc.<ref name="Blood of the Empire 1" /> He appears again in [[The Old Republic, Blood of the Empire Act 3: Burn the Future|''Act 3: Burn the Future'']],<ref name="Blood of the Empire 3" /> and is featured in several flashbacks in the early issues of [[Star Wars: The Old Republic — The Lost Suns|''The Lost Suns'']] story arc&mdash;most notably on the cover of [[The Old Republic — The Lost Suns 2|''The Lost Suns, Part 2'']].<ref name="The Lost Suns">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic — The Lost Suns]]''</ref>

Darth Marr appears in the finales of both the Sith Warrior and Sith Inquisitor storylines in ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', the [[Wikipedia:Massively multiplayer online role-playing game|massively multiplayer online role-playing game]] released by [[BioWare]] and [[LucasArts]] on [[December 20]], [[2011]]. In the Sith Warrior finale, "Retribution", Marr occupies the throne third from the left on the left hand side of the chamber.<ref name="Retribution" /> However, in the Sith Inquisitor finale "The Dark Council", Marr is instead seated on the far right throne on the left-hand side.<ref name="The Dark Council" />

In post-class story content for ''The Old Republic'', Darth Marr becomes a major NPC, assuming a leadership role in the Empire and acting as the immediate superior and quest-giver for Imperial players (a role filled by Satele Shan and [[Leontyne Saresh]] for the Republic).

Darth Marr is voiced by [[Michael Harney]].
